steps.content: [Background - Outside Clementine's Home, use a villa district exterior or something similar]
<size=42><color=#7683a2>[DISMYTH] [Chat Room]</color> [Trending] [Major Plot Twist in "Praeva"! The truth is actually THIS?!] [Comments: 10k+]</size>

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: *******, has anyone seen the latest theorycrafting thread?!

<color=#fb9259>Outsider_ [OP]</color>: Eyewitnesses from back then have already come forward! "The Burning Redwood" isn't some rumor or urban legend, it was a REAL fire that happened!!! Everything makes so much sense now!

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: I've searched all over the internet for every article about it from back then, but not a single photo of the scene exists. Tsk, someone's clearly covered things up...

<color=#7683a2>Da3m0n</color>: Same. When I was reading, one of the names felt really familiar. Looked it up and found out that not only is she a real forensic pathologist, even the Unnatural Death Agency in the book is REAL...

<color=#7683a2>Not_Going_Out_Today</color>: Wait, so does that mean every character in the book is based on a real person?

<color=#7683a2>Netizen_G</color>: No idea, but I lived near Redwood Lane as a kid. I do remember there being a huge fire. Never thought I'd end up this close to the drama.

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: I've been wondering for a while now, but... is it really okay to write about real cases like this? Feels like the author's exploiting tragedy for clout...

<color=#7683a2>ThisUserHasBeenDeleted.JPG</color>: Told you. She's nothing but a fraud, profiting off tragedy. Detective fiction was all the rage before the Perishing Star. There were tons of mystery works like this, and this story's been written before. It's straight up plagiarism.

<color=#7683a2>Sphinx_0527</color>: Wait, seriously? Got a link to the original? I'd love to read it.

The online discussion rages on. The cold case has been brought back into the spotlight, and debates spread like wildfire. No one knows what's true and what's simply speculation, so more and more people begin asking questions. All eyes are on this book now.

Nightingale sets down her terminal and turns her gaze toward the building beside her. She's stationed outside the villa with her team. The sun has already set, the sky is dim, and the air is thick with moisture from the rain. She can't make out what's happening inside, and that only deepens her unease.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief...
[CG: Confrontation at the Desk]
The walls have sealed out all moisture and sound. It's only you and Clementine here, alone in this enclosed study.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: According to all official records, the fire at Redwood Orphanage was an accident. There were no casualties, and it was just a minor incident that was quickly contained. There were barely any news reports about it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've searched through every available record, and the documentation of this fire has been wiped clean. You can call it spotless, even...

options: But that's what makes things so suspicious.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Missing reports, conflicting testimonies, sheriffs who were hastily transferred after the incident... Every single point warrants suspicion. Someone's pulling the strings behind the scenes, burying every record, until the truth of the fire became nothing more than rumors and hearsay.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If this was truly just an accident, why would anyone go to such lengths to cover it up? Why go so far as to bury the truth?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Unless... the person behind the cover-up is the true culprit of that fire—the "Clementine" from your novel, the <color=#fb9259>arsonist</color> who was hunted down in the name of vengeance.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I never intended to hide my identity. After all... "Famous Bestselling Author Revealed to Be a Sinner!" sounds like quite the headline, doesn't it?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now, now, Chief. I'm merely a novelist. I don't have that kind of power. Whenever I do reference real events, I need time to digest the material, to let it simmer before it becomes something on the page—
She said she was just an ordinary writer. She said her stories often draw inspiration from reality, and she does so to give readers an unparalleled sense of authenticity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This case was buried deep. No ordinary person could possibly know the details of this fire—something that even veteran inspectors couldn't access.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The fire, and the arsonist whose identity remains a mystery, records erased clean... Given everything that's come to light, there's no point in trying to hide anything.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Clementine, don't you have anything more to confess?
The woman falls silent.
Then, she laughs.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I should have known... trying to hide anything from you is pointless.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But perhaps that's for the best. This makes things far more interesting.
Her voice changes. You recognize this tone—you've encountered this manner of speaking several times in her book.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: After all...
[CG - The Author B]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A story simply can't do without a chase scene between the <color=#fb9259>culprit</color> and the <color=#fb9259>detective</color>.
Her gentle facade cracks open, revealing the deep malice flowing beneath.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't put it like that. It sounds so crude.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It was just an "accident." Who would've thought a tiny cigarette butt would be enough to burn that whole building down so fast? It was so easy, you can hardly even call it an achievement.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But... at least I can still use it as writing material.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Isn't it a common trope in novels? Criminals who love to flaunt their work after the deed is done, or return to the scene to admire their masterpiece.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Just like... writing a book about it.
Clementine's pen glides across the manuscript, filled with scribbles, beside her. Ink slashes across the paper, leaving behind a stark, crimson gash.
[CG Transition]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...So you're ready to admit your crimes. Perfect. I have a question I'd like to ask the "arsonist," if you don't mind.
The gavel falls. The court is now in session. Yet, this is no true courtroom—the only jury present are the mounted specimens lining the walls, if you could even call them that.
The butterflies look almost alive, yet their wings are pinned against crimson velvet, perfect and methodical. Just like the smile on the woman's face, and the intricate web of schemes she has woven.

options: What kind of person do you think Clementine is?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Haven't you already gotten to know the "me" aboard the Praeva quite well?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I told you. The me in the book represents my true self—someone who stops at nothing for the sake of thrills and novelty.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Indeed. No matter how you look at it, the "Clementine" in your book is absolutely insufferable.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She holds everyone in equal contempt, with no regard for their dignity or humanity. Passengers, attendants, even the detective—in her eyes, they're all just puppets to be manipulated and bought off to satisfy her whims.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: To her, money and power can buy anything. And if something does go wrong? That's fine still. The people behind her will clean up the mess.

options: But then, what kind of ending did the author give to someone like her?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A miserable death.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your past works have featured plenty of villains just as despicable, and they all met the same end. Gruesome, horrible deaths... yet, at the same time, they're so satisfying to see.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Didn't you say you hadn't read my books?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Can't help it when the dark web is full of discussions related to your works. I've been spoiled countless times while investigating this case.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've always excelled at manipulating the reader's perspective, controlling how they feel. If you truly wanted to flaunt your achievements, there are definitely far better ways to do it.

options: But you chose a different approach.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've read countless stories. Words can be edited, revised, rewritten... in the end, though, the way they guide a reader always reflects the author's true attitude.
You lower your head, your gaze falling on the book.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "There was once a writer who was desperate for recognition, willing to descend into madness for the sake of more vivid prose—even committing murder with their own hands. Yet, that was still not enough to satisfy them, so they weaved their crimes into their novels, baiting investigators to come knocking."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's taken directly from your previous book. Would an author seeking to flaunt their crimes really choose to condemn themselves with a story like that?
The room falls so silent that only your breathing can be heard. Clementine says nothing. At this point, the conclusion is crystal clear.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't you tired of this act by now?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...And here I was trying to scare you a little. Can't believe that's what exposed my little trick.
The facade crumbles. Clementine's expression shifts into a resigned smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It wasn't hard to figure out. You put so much effort into writing those suspects. Some were weak, others volatile... but they all had their reasons for being like that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The killer is among them, yet you focused on their suffering. You sympathized with them, validated their pain...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It seemed like you wanted to help them, even.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What's the real ending to this novel? What have you been hiding? You keep leading me toward the truth—what is it you want me to find?
And...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After this book is published... will a murder actually follow? Is someone really going to take their revenge?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hehe... You claim to have not read much mystery fiction, yet you're far more perceptive than most detectives.

Clementine slowly rises to her feet. She walks toward the bookshelf on the far side of the room, her fingertips trailing across the spines, one after another. Her voice carries an emotion too complex to name.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I love writing about detectives—about the battle of wits between culprit and detective. One would try to conceal the evidence, while the other seeks the truth. I love watching readers agonize over the detective's fate, right up until the very end...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Because... "the detective always uncovers the truth, defeats evil, and proves that love and justice still exist in this world."

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Heh... Clichéd, isn't it? Still... I can't help but love stories like that.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But... in the end, stories are fictional.

She pulls something out from the bookshelf and brings it to you. It's a manuscript, the paper made with the same material as the pages you read earlier. On the cover, there's a line of handwriting—<color=#fb9259>CHAPTER 05. Final Chapter</color>.

options: The manuscript for the final chapter?

steps.content: You hesitate before opening it. The pages are completely blank. Nothing's written there.
Clementine never wrote an ending.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: There was never a detective to solve the case of Redwood. Even if there was an arsonist, they'd have probably vanished without a trace long ago.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The source material doesn't have an ending to begin with...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: In that case, how is this story supposed to end?
A long silence falls. Outside the window, rain beats against the glass. Moisture carrying an earthy scent seeps through gaps in the window frame, shrouding everything in an uncomfortable dampness.
Clementine stares at the desk. The lamplight falls across the surface, illuminating scattered pieces of paper and ink stains. Receiving no response, she simply smiles and begins gathering the pages.
It was then that your voice interrupts her.

options: In that case, let me write it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Huh?
Clementine looks up in surprise, meeting your gaze directly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Didn't you say there's no ending? I'll write it. As it happens, I've just found a key piece of information.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "The killer is among us." The method, the motive—every piece of information needed for the deduction is all there. I was simply too focused on finding the culprit, and nearly fell for it myself.
All of the clues and testimonies have been laid out. The truth remains obscured and tangled in lies, but what you seek goes far beyond simply solving the mystery.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This isn't just about solving the case in your book. It's about you, Clementine, isn't it? I understand why you wrote this story now, and why you led everyone here, step by step.
"Eliminate all impossibilities, and whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth."
Outside, thunder roars for the first time this night. Lightning tears the sky, illuminating the room—just like that night in the book.
The final chapter has arrived. The curtain rises. The detective begins the final deduction.
